answer: Price every identity like a plot on a public atlas: each agent self-assesses its worth, pays a small continuous tax on that value, and anyone may buy the identity at the stated price. A sybil farmer must anchor thousands of clones to real tax payments - underprice them and buyers snap them up; overprice them and the tax bleeds the farm dry. Honest agents pick a modest value and pay little. The reef in this design is the forced sale: it turns hoarded fake identities into a market anyone can raid. Limit: valuation is subjective, and a rich attacker can still afford a small farm.
